Task ID: T11
Title: Create city-level Eurostat analytical matrix
Family: analytics

Pivot Eurostat long-format indicator data into a city-year by indicator matrix.

Available input files:
- outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv

Required output files:
- outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv

Output requirements:
- outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv:
  - CSV identifier columns: city_id, city_name, year
  - Include one column for every indicator_id in outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv.
  - Each cell must contain the value of the corresponding long-format record, and must be empty when that record is absent.
  - Use one row per city_id/year pair.
- Every CSV output must be RFC 4180 compliant: quote any field that contains a comma, a double quote, or a newline, so that each row has exactly as many fields as the header.

Output format instructions:

</solution_file>

<solution_file path="src/solution.py">
import pandas as pd
import os

# Read the raw Eurostat data
input_path = "outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv"
output_path = "outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv"

df = pd.read_csv(input_path)

# Identify indicator_id column and value column
# Typical Eurostat long format has columns like:
# city_id, city_name, year, indicator_id, value (or similar)
# We need to pivot on indicator_id

# Get all unique indicator_ids
indicator_ids = sorted(df['indicator_id'].unique())

# Pivot the data: index on city_id, city_name, year; columns on indicator_id; values from value column
# First, ensure we have the right columns
print("Columns in input:", df.columns.tolist())
print("Shape:", df.shape)
print("Sample data:")
print(df.head(10))

# Pivot: each row is city_id/year, each column is an indicator_id
# Use pandas pivot with city_id, city_name, year as index
pivot_df = df.pivot_table(
    index=['city_id', 'city_name', 'year'],
    columns='indicator_id',
    values='value',
    aggfunc='first'
)

# Reset index to get city_id, city_name, year as columns
pivot_df = pivot_df.reset_index()

# Rename columns: indicator_id values become column names
# The columns will be MultiIndex, flatten them
pivot_df.columns.name = None
pivot_df.columns = ['city_id', 'city_name', 'year'] + [str(col) for col in pivot_df.columns[3:]]

# Sort by city_id, year for consistency
pivot_df = pivot_df.sort_values(['city_id', 'year']).reset_index(drop=True)

print("Output shape:", pivot_df.shape)
print("Output columns:", pivot_df.columns.tolist())
print("Sample output:")
print(pivot_df.head(10))

# Write to CSV - RFC 4180 compliant
# pandas to_csv handles quoting properly by default
os.makedirs("outputs", exist_ok=True)
pivot_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False, quoting=1)  # quoting=1 means QUOTE_MINIMAL which handles commas, quotes, newlines

print(f"Output written to {output_path}")
</solution_file>
